_comment: Version strings that cve-bin-tool's signature checkers do not pick up.
cve-bin-tool requires a fixed string and regex per component, and misses a
component whose binary spells its version some other way — a three-digit
requirement drops `FFmpeg version 4.1`, a CLI-only marker drops a library
build. This table adds those forms. It does not replace cve-bin-tool; the
merge keeps whichever judgement already exists.
The name set is deliberately closed. An open `<name> <version>` pattern over a
firmware rootfs returns IP addresses, netmasks, XMP namespaces, PDF versions,
HTTP/1.1 and cross-toolchain paths by the hundred — measured on the corpus
before this table was written. Every entry below was verified against a real
About `cpe`: null means no CPE is attached, and the component is then worth
the same as a presence-only judgement for vulnerability purposes. That is the
honest outcome when the identity is not settled — a wrong CPE hands the
component another project's advisories. Every non-null vendor:product here
exists in the bundled NVD CPE index; the Dockerfile fails the build if one
does not, so the table cannot drift away from the index it is matched against.

entries.name: net-tools
entries.why: No net-tools product exists anywhere in the NVD CPE index, so there is nothing to attach. Reported for the licence obligation only.

entries.name: netkit-ftp
entries.why: netkit stamps an RCS keyword of its own, `$NetKit: <package>-<version> $`, which no checker looks for. The whole keyword is matched rather than the bare name so a mention of the package elsewhere cannot stand in for it, and the pattern names ftp specifically because the same keyword form is used by every netkit tool. The prerelease suffix is captured rather than trimmed: 0.18-pre1 precedes 0.18, and reporting it as 0.18 would claim a release the image does not carry. Identity is settled here, unlike net-tools and hydra, so the CPE is attached.

entries.name: hydra
entries.why: Five unrelated products are called hydra in the NVD index (hydrairc, ory, nixos, iohk, hydra_project), and this string is an HTTP `Server:` banner emitted by a web server binary, not the THC-Hydra tool. Any CPE here would hand it another project's advisories. The vendor's own notice declares `hydra`, so the name is reported and the identifier is not.

entries.name: uclibc
entries.why: uClibc names its shared object after the upstream version, which is the one place a filename may be read as one. The CPE is left off because two projects claim the name — uclibc:uclibc ended at 0.9.33 and uclibc-ng_project:uclibc-ng picks up at 1.0 — and deciding between them from a filename alone is a guess.

entries.name: ffmpeg
entries.why: cve-bin-tool's checker wants three digits and so drops the two-digit form this string uses. ffmpeg:ffmpeg is the only sensible product in the index and carries the overwhelming majority of ffmpeg advisories.
entries.where: an iOS app bundle, `FFmpeg version 4.1-QtAV`; the file is no longer in the corpus, so this entry is covered by a fixture rather than by a live scan
